thread.title: Apple In Buy Range As Nasdaq, Chips Lead Stock Market Rebound

author: DAVID SAITO-CHUNG
title: Apple In Buy Range As Nasdaq, Chips Lead Stock Market Rebound
text:
Investors hopped back into stocks today even after a U.S. government official told Bloomberg there's a 99% chance that the U.S. on Friday will start imposing tariffs on billions of dollars' worth of Chinese products. Apple helped the Nasdaq pace the major indexes with a nearly 1.1% gain as of 3:45 p.m. ET, while the S&P 500 was not far behind, rising more than 0.8%.
X At 2736, the S&P 500 is up 2.3% since Jan. 1, following a 19.4% lift in 2017.
The Nasdaq, at 7585, has advanced 9.9% year to date. In 2017, the premier index for growth companies vaulted 28.2% higher.
Apple ( AAPL ), up 9.4% for the year, as well as chip companies spearheaded the Nasdaq's outperformance. The iPhone, iPad and digital services titan rallied nearly 0.9% and is holding up above its rising 50-day moving average, a good sign for the bulls.
Apple: $911 Billion Market Cap The megacap tech, which sports a $911 billion market cap, stands 3.6% above the 179.04 buy point in a seven-week double bottom. Apple initially broke out on May 4, thrusting nearly 4% higher in volume that jumped 61% above the 50-day average.
Therefore, Apple stands within the important 5% buy zone .
Also watch for a potential base on base to also possibly form.
Apple sports a decent Relative Price Strength Rating of 79 on a scale of 1 to 99, according to IBD Stock Checkup . That scores trails industry compatriots Roku ( ROKU ), Ooma ( OOMA ) and Motorola Solutions ( MSI ) within IBD's Telecom-Consumer Products industry group.
Roku went public at 14 a share on Sept. 28 last year, then rocketed out of a first-stage IPO base at 29.90 six weeks later. That breakout yielded a solid gain of 96%.
Apple Vs. Roku: Tale Of The Stock Tape Roku peaked a 58.80, then dived into its current cup-type base.
While the Los Gatos, Calif., company shows formidable revenue growth (up 29% in 2017 to $513 million), Roku is not expected to go fully into the black until 2019. It's expected to lose 29 cents a share this year, then earn 5 cents a share next year.
Apple, in turn, continues to forge a path of growth acceleration.
The Street sees earnings climbing 31% to $2.18 a share in the June-ended fiscal third quarter. That would exceed its year-over-year increases of 11%, 18%, 24%, 16% and 30% in the prior five quarters.
Apple's revenue, driven in large part by fantastic growth of digital services and brand-new product innovations such as the cellular-ready Apple Watch, is seen rising 15% to $52.3 billion.
The Dow Jones industrial average lagged the other main indexes, rising 0.7%. The S&P SmallCap 600 rallied 0.8%.
Top industry groups of the day not only included the chip sector. While some defensive areas of the market, such as dairy products, confectionery foods, meat and household appliances, all rose sharply, steel production, tires, solar, movie and steel alloy firms also gained 1.9% or higher.
When To Buy Intel At least nine of the 30 components in the Dow industrial average have gained 1 point or more, including chipmaking giant Intel ( INTC ). The stock rallied nearly 2% to 50.42 in below-average trade and lies 12% below a 52-week peak of 57.60.
The member of IBD's semiconductor manufacturing industry group is caught in a type of "no man's land," chart-wise. As seen in a daily chart, the stock has fallen well below its 50-day moving average. That triggered a sell signal for recent new investors. However, Intel is also keeping an air cushion above the long-term 200-day moving average. That signals the stock's long-term run is not over.
Please go to the charts in MarketSmith to see both the 50- and 200-day moving averages in action.
For now, keep watching how the stock acts and see if it has the strength to build a new base and thus furnish a new correct buy opportunity .
Second-quarter results look positive. The Street sees Intel's earnings galloping 32% higher to 95 cents a share on a 13% increase in sales to $16.69 billion. In the first quarter, Intel grew EPS 32% and the top line 9%.
Datacenter revenue has become an ever more important part of the business pie for Intel.
ASML ( ASML ), a lithography systems expert and member of the chip equipment group, has performed in a similar fashion technically. The Dutch giant, up 2.2% to 195.85, is sandwiched in between its 50- and 200-day lines. However, the stock lies just 9% below a 216.90 all-time peak.
Watch This Number Earnings at ASML grew 74%, 115%, 34%, 46%, 39% and 38% vs. year-ago levels in the past six quarters. Analysts surveyed by Thomson Reuters see earnings up just 4% in Q2 to $1.28 a share.
In other financial markets, crude oil dropped hard as Iran reportedly told President Trump to stop tweeting about energy prices. WTI near-term futures fell 1.3% to $73.16 a barrel. At that level, however, WTI is down less than 3% from its 52-week peak of $75.27.
